headline: A KPMG survey of 400 chief executives of big US companies found about nine in ten expect to hire more people over the next three years despite AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a survey of expectations, not of actual hiring.
importance_line: Job seekers get an upbeat signal, but it records what bosses say they expect, not what they actually do.
summary: Business Insider reports on a survey by KPMG US, the American arm of the accounting and consulting firm, of 400 chief executives of large US companies: about nine in ten expect to increase headcount over the next three years, and three-quarters say AI has made them reassess the skills needed for entry-level jobs. Only 9 percent describe AI agents as “transformational” for their organizations today.
notes: Axios (the pool source) was blocked; entry written from Business Insider. The Axios link is in the pool. Quote from KPMG US chair Tim Walsh not used.
